title.en: "I am a student": pronouns and the "to be" endings

body.en:
Uzbek has no separate verb "to be". Instead, a personal ending is added to the word: [[Men talabaman.]] = I am a student.

PronounEndingExample
[[men]] I-man[[talabaman]]
[[sen]] you-san[[talabasan]]
[[u]] he/she—[[talaba]]
[[biz]] we-miz[[talabamiz]]
[[siz]] you (polite/plural)-siz[[talabasiz]]
[[ular]] they-(lar)[[talabalar]]

For "not", use [[emas]], which takes the ending: [[Men shifokor emasman.]] = I am not a doctor.

grammar.ex:
Men talabaman.|I am a student.
Sen shifokorsan.|You are a doctor.
U oʻqituvchi.|He is a teacher.
Biz doʻstmiz.|We are friends.
Men charchagan emasman.|I am not tired.

body.en:
The plural is easy: add [[-lar]] to any noun: [[kitob]] → [[kitoblar]] (books), [[bola]] → [[bolalar]] (children).

"My, your, his" are endings on the noun:

after a consonantafter a vowel
my[[kitobim]][[onam]]
your[[kitobing]][[onang]]
his/her[[kitobi]][[onasi]]
our[[kitobimiz]][[onamiz]]
your (pl.)[[kitobingiz]][[onangiz]]

You can add the pronoun for emphasis: [[mening kitobim]] = my book.

grammar.ex:
Bu mening kitobim.|This is my book.
Onam uyda.|My mother is at home.
Bolalar maktabda.|The children are at school.
Ismingiz nima?|What is your name?

body.en:
For a yes/no question, add [[-mi]] to the word you are asking about: [[Bu choy.]] → [[Bu choymi?]] (Is this tea?)

Question words: [[nima]] what, [[kim]] who, [[qayerda]] where, [[qayerga]] where to, [[qachon]] when, [[qanday]] how, [[qancha]] how much, [[nega]] why.

With a question word, -mi is not used: [[Bu nima?]] = What is this?

grammar.ex:
Siz talabamisiz?|Are you a student?
Bu nima?|What is this?
U kim?|Who is he?
Bozor qayerda?|Where is the market?
Bu qancha turadi?|How much does this cost?

title.en: bor and yoʻq: "there is" and "I have"

body.en:
[[bor]] = there is; [[yoʻq]] = there isn't: [[Uyda non bor.]] = There is bread at home.

"I have" = possessive ending + bor: [[Mening mashinam bor.]] = I have a car (literally "my car exists").

To ask: [[bormi?]] — [[Vaqtingiz bormi?]] = Do you have time?

grammar.ex:
Mening akam bor.|I have an older brother.
Uyda non yoʻq.|There is no bread at home.
Vaqtingiz bormi?|Do you have time?
Bu yerda bank bormi?|Is there a bank here?

Men olma, pomidor va bodring sotib olaman.|I buy apples, tomatoes and cucumbers.
Sotuvchi juda mehribon.|The seller is very kind.
U: «Assalomu alaykum! Nima kerak?» — deydi.|He says: "Hello! What would you like?"
Men: «Bir kilo uzum, iltimos», — deb javob beraman.|I answer: "A kilo of grapes, please."

Yana non, pishloq va asal olaman.|I also buy bread, cheese and honey.
Keyin uyga borib, salat tayyorlayman.|Then I go home and make a salad.

Instead of prepositions, Uzbek uses endings:

EndingMeaningExample
-nidefinite object[[kitobni oʻqiyman]]
-gato[[maktabga]]
-dain / at[[uyda]]
-danfrom[[Toshkentdan]]
-ningof / 's[[akamning uyi]]

After k, -ga becomes -ka; after q it becomes -qa: [[bankka]], [[qishloqqa]].

grammar.ex:
Men kitobni oʻqiyman.|I'm reading the book.
Biz maktabga boramiz.|We go to school.
U Toshkentda yashaydi.|He lives in Tashkent.
Men Iordaniyadanman.|I am from Jordan.
Bu akamning uyi.|This is my brother's house.

body.en:
One tense covers both habits and the future: verb stem + [[-a]] (after a consonant) or [[-y]] (after a vowel) + personal ending.

bor- (go)o'qi- (read)
I[[boraman]][[oʻqiyman]]
you[[borasan]][[oʻqiysan]]
he/she[[boradi]][[oʻqiydi]]
we[[boramiz]][[oʻqiymiz]]
you (pl.)[[borasiz]][[oʻqiysiz]]
they[[borishadi]][[oʻqishadi]]

[[Har kuni ishlayman]] = I work every day; [[Ertaga kelaman]] = I'll come tomorrow — the same form.

grammar.ex:
Men har kuni ishlayman.|I work every day.
Ertaga kelaman.|I'll come tomorrow.
U rus tilini biladi.|He knows Russian.
Biz choy ichamiz.|We drink tea.

body.en:
Past tense = stem + [[-di]] + a short personal ending:

Iyouheweyou (pl.)they
[[bordim]][[bording]][[bordi]][[bordik]][[bordingiz]][[borishdi]]

Note: "we" ends in -k in the past ([[keldik]] = we came) but in -miz in the present ([[kelamiz]]).

grammar.ex:
Kecha kinoga bordim.|Yesterday I went to the cinema.
Biz osh yedik.|We ate plov.
Siz qachon keldingiz?|When did you arrive?
U uyga qaytdi.|He went back home.

body.en:
To negate a verb, put [[-ma-]] right after the stem: [[boraman]] → [[bormayman]] (I won't go / I don't go), [[bordim]] → [[bormadim]] (I didn't go).

To negate a noun or adjective, use [[emas]]: [[Bu qimmat emas.]] = It isn't expensive.

In the present, -ma- + -y-: [[tushunmayman]] = I don't understand.

grammar.ex:
Men goʻsht yemayman.|I don't eat meat.
U kelmadi.|He didn't come.
Bu qimmat emas.|It isn't expensive.
Men tushunmayman.|I don't understand.

For what is happening right now, use [[-yap-]] + personal ending: [[oʻqiyapman]] = I'm reading now.

He/she: [[-yapti]]: [[Yomgʻir yogʻyapti.]] = It's raining.

Compare: [[Har kuni ishlayman]] (habit) — [[Hozir ishlayapman]] (right now).

grammar.ex:
Hozir ishlayapman.|I'm working now.
Yomgʻir yogʻyapti.|It's raining.
Nima qilyapsan?|What are you doing?
Biz sizni kutyapmiz.|We are waiting for you.

body.en:
"I want to / I'm going to" = stem + [[-moqchi]] + personal ending: [[bormoqchiman]] = I want to go.

Negative: [[bormoqchi emasman]] = I don't intend to go.

You can also use [[xohlamoq]] (to want): [[Choy xohlaysizmi?]] = Would you like some tea?

grammar.ex:
Men shifokor boʻlmoqchiman.|I want to become a doctor.
Ertaga bozorga bormoqchimiz.|We're going to the market tomorrow.
U uy sotib olmoqchi.|He wants to buy a house.

body.en:
"Can" = stem + [[-a]]/[[-y]] + the verb [[olmoq]], conjugated: [[gapira olaman]] = I can speak.

The negative goes on olmoq: [[kela olmadim]] = I couldn't come.

grammar.ex:
Men oʻzbekcha gapira olaman.|I can speak Uzbek.
Kecha kela olmadim.|I couldn't come yesterday.
Menga yordam bera olasizmi?|Can you help me?

body.en:
"I have to" = verb in [[-ish]] + possessive ending + [[kerak]]: [[borishim kerak]] = I have to go (literally "my going is needed").

"I need something" = [[Menga ... kerak]]: [[Menga yordam kerak.]] = I need help.

Negative: [[kerak emas]] = not necessary.

grammar.ex:
Men ishga borishim kerak.|I have to go to work.
Sizga nima kerak?|What do you need?
Shoshilish kerak emas.|There's no need to hurry.

readings.title: Birinchi ish kuni
readings.sents:
Birinchi ish kuni har doim hayajonli boʻladi.|The first working day is always exciting.
Ofisga hammadan oldin, soat sakkizda keldim.|I came to the office before everyone, at eight o'clock.
Boshliq meni kutib oldi va hamkasblarim bilan tanishtirdi.|The boss met me and introduced me to my colleagues.
Hamma juda samimiy edi.|Everyone was very friendly.
Menga ish joyim va kompyuterimni koʻrsatishdi.|They showed me my workplace and computer.
Avvaliga hujjatlarni oʻqidim va loyihalarni oʻrgandim.|At first I read documents and studied projects.
Tushlikda birga oshxonaga bordik.|At lunch we went to the canteen together.
Tushlikdan keyin majlisimiz boʻldi.|After lunch we had a meeting.
Biroz hayajonlandim, lekin hammasi yaxshi oʻtdi.|I was a bit nervous, but everything went well.
Kechqurun charchagan, lekin mamnun edim.|In the evening I was tired but satisfied.
Oʻylaymanki, bu yer menga yoqadi.|I think I'm going to like it here.

readings.title: Sogʻlom turmush tarzi
readings.sents:
Hozir koʻp odamlar sogʻligʻi haqida oʻylaydi.|Nowadays many people think about their health.
Shifokorlar koʻproq harakat qilishni maslahat berishadi.|Doctors advise moving more.
Kuniga kamida yarim soat piyoda yurish foydali.|It is useful to walk at least half an hour a day.
Toʻgʻri ovqatlanish ham muhim.|It is also important to eat properly.
Koʻproq sabzavot va meva yeyish kerak.|You need to eat more vegetables and fruit.
Shirin ichimliklar emas, suv ichgan yaxshi.|It's better to drink water, not sweet drinks.
Uyqu ham juda muhim.|Sleep is also very important.
Kattalarga yetti-sakkiz soat uxlash kerak.|An adult needs to sleep seven to eight hours.
Va, albatta, chekmaslik kerak.|And, of course, you shouldn't smoke.
Sogʻliq eng muhim narsa.|Health is the most important thing.

readings.title: Men oʻzbek tilini qanday oʻrganyapman
readings.sents:
Men oʻzbek tilini bir yildan beri oʻrganyapman.|I have been learning Uzbek for a year already.
Avvaliga juda qiyin edi.|At first it was very hard.
Qoʻshimchalarni tushunmasdim va ularni aralashtirib yuborardim.|I didn't understand the cases and mixed up the endings.
Keyin har kuni podkastlar tinglashni boshladim.|Then I started listening to podcasts every day.
Filmlarni subtitrlar bilan ham koʻraman.|I also watch films with subtitles.
Oʻzbek doʻstlarim menga juda koʻp yordam berishdi.|My Uzbek friends helped me a lot.
Ular xatolarimni tuzatishadi va kulishmaydi.|They correct my mistakes and don't laugh.
Endi doʻkonda ham, ishda ham gaplasha olaman.|Now I can speak at the shop and at work.
Eng muhimi — xatolardan qoʻrqmaslik.|The main thing is not to be afraid of mistakes.

body.en:
"If" = stem + [[-sa]] + a short ending: [[kelsam]] (if I come), [[kelsang]], [[kelsa]], [[kelsak]], [[kelsangiz]].

For unreal conditions ("if I had…, I would…"): [[-sa]] ... [[-ar edi]]: [[Pulim boʻlsa, sayohat qilardim.]] = If I had money, I would travel.

grammar.ex:
Vaqtim boʻlsa, kelaman.|If I have time, I'll come.
Yomgʻir yogʻsa, uyda qolamiz.|If it rains, we'll stay home.
Pulim boʻlsa, sayohat qilardim.|If I had money, I would travel.

quiz.en: "If I had known, I would have told you":

body.en:
Uzbek has no word for "which/who". Put the verb in [[-gan]] before the noun: [[men oʻqigan kitob]] = the book (that) I read.

With a personal ending, -gan expresses experience: [[Samarqandga borganman.]] = I have been to Samarkand.

grammar.ex:
Men oʻqigan kitob juda qiziq.|The book I read is very interesting.
Bu men tugʻilgan shahar.|This is the city where I was born.
Imtihonni topshirgan talaba mamnun.|The student who passed the exam is happy.
Men Samarqandga borganman.|I have been to Samarkand.

body.en:
Add [[-il-]] after the stem (or [[-in-]] if the stem ends in l or a vowel): [[qurmoq]] (to build) → [[qurildi]] (was built), [[oʻqimoq]] → [[oʻqiladi]] (is read).

[[Bu yerda chekilmaydi.]] = There's no smoking here.

grammar.ex:
Koʻprik oʻtgan asrda qurilgan.|The bridge was built last century.
Xat kecha yuborildi.|The letter was sent yesterday.
Bu kitob koʻp tillarga tarjima qilingan.|This book has been translated into many languages.

readings.title: Kelajak shahri
readings.sents:
Kelajak shahri qanday boʻladi?|What will the city of the future be like?
Koʻp mutaxassislar unda koʻkalamzorlar koʻp, mashinalar kam boʻladi deb oʻylaydi.|Many experts think it will have more greenery and fewer cars.
Odamlar elektromobillar va velosipedlarda yuradi.|People will travel by electric cars and bicycles.
Uylar energiyani quyosh va shamoldan oladi.|Homes will get energy from the sun and wind.
Aqlli tizimlar yorugʻlik va issiqlikni boshqaradi.|Smart systems will control light and heat.
Biroq bu gʻoyaning tanqidchilari ham bor.|However, this idea also has critics.
Ular bunday texnologiyalar juda qimmat deyishadi.|They say such technologies are too expensive.
Bundan tashqari, hamma ham odatlarini oʻzgartirishga tayyor emas.|Besides, not everyone is ready to change their habits.
Kim haq ekanini aytish qiyin.|It's hard to say who is right.
Ammo bir narsa aniq: shahar odamlar uchun qulay boʻlishi kerak.|But one thing is clear: a city must be comfortable for people.

readings.title: Ijtimoiy tarmoqlar
readings.sents:
Ijtimoiy tarmoqlar hayotimizning bir qismiga aylandi.|Social networks have become part of our lives.
Ular uzoqda yashovchi doʻstlar bilan muloqot qilishga yordam beradi.|They help us communicate with friends who live far away.
Yangiliklarni avvalgidan tezroq bilib olamiz.|We learn the news faster than before.
Biroq ijtimoiy tarmoqlarning salbiy tomoni ham bor.|However, social networks also have a downside.
Koʻp odamlar kuniga bir necha soatni telefonda oʻtkazadi.|Many people spend several hours a day on their phones.
Bu uyqu, oʻqish va kayfiyatga taʼsir qiladi.|This affects sleep, studies and mood.
Bundan tashqari, internetda feyklar koʻp.|In addition, there is a lot of fake news online.
Psixologlar tanaffus qilishni maslahat beradi.|Psychologists advise taking breaks.
Masalan, telefonni yotoqxonaga olib kirmaslik mumkin.|For example, you can avoid taking the phone into the bedroom.
Asosiysi — hayot ekranda oʻtmasligini yodda tutish.|The main thing is to remember that life doesn't happen on a screen.

Endi u yerga birga boramiz.|Now we go there together.

A|Men qishloqda yashashni xohlardim. U yer tinch va havosi toza.|I would like to live in the countryside. It's quiet there and the air is clean.
B|Lekin shaharda imkoniyatlar koʻproq.|But there are more opportunities in the city.
A|Masalan?|Such as?
B|Ish, yaxshi maktablar, kasalxonalar, teatrlar.|Jobs, good schools, hospitals, theaters.
A|Qoʻshilaman, lekin shaharda stress va tirbandlik koʻp.|I agree, but the city has a lot of stress and traffic jams.
B|Bu toʻgʻri. Balki shahar chekkasida yashagan maʼqulmi?|That's true. Maybe it's best to live in the suburbs?
A|Yaxshi fikr! Tabiat yaqin, shahar ham uzoq emas.|Good idea! Nature is nearby and the city isn't far.
B|Demak, kelishdik.|So we agree.

A|Xoʻsh, film senga qanday yoqdi?|So how did you like the film?
B|Rostini aytsam, koʻproq narsa kutgandim.|To be honest, I expected more.
A|Rostdanmi? Menga yoqdi. Aktyorlar ajoyib oʻynashdi.|Really? I liked it. The actors played beautifully.
B|Bunga qoʻshilaman. Lekin syujet juda oldindan bilinardi.|I agree with that. But the plot was too predictable.
A|Lekin yakuni kutilmagan boʻldi.|But the ending was unexpected.
B|Balki. Musiqasi ham yaxshi edi.|Perhaps. The music was good too.
A|Keyingi safar filmni sen tanlaysan.|Next time you choose the film.
B|Kelishdik!|Deal!

A|Ayting-chi, biznesingizni qanday boshlagansiz?|Tell us, how did you start your business?
B|Hammasi kichik gʻoya va katta istakdan boshlandi.|It all started with a small idea and a big desire.
A|Qiyin boʻldimi?|Was it difficult?
B|Juda. Birinchi yili zarar bilan ishladik.|Very. In the first year we worked at a loss.
A|Taslim boʻlmaslikka nima yordam berdi?|What helped you not to give up?
B|Oilamning qoʻllab-quvvatlashi va mahsulotimga ishonch.|My family's support and faith in my product.
A|Yosh tadbirkorlarga nima maslahat berasiz?|What would you advise young entrepreneurs?
B|Xatolardan qoʻrqmaslik va ulardan saboq olish.|Not to be afraid of mistakes and to learn from them.

body.en:
To link actions in sequence, put the first verb in [[-ib]] (-b after a vowel) and conjugate only the last: [[Uyga kelib, ovqatlandim.]] = I came home and ate.

[[-ayotib]] = "while": [[Uyga qaytayotib, doʻstimni uchratdim.]] = While returning home, I met my friend.

grammar.ex:
Maqolani oʻqib, u fikrini oʻzgartirdi.|Having read the article, he changed his mind.
Uyga qaytayotib, eski doʻstimni uchratdim.|On my way home I met an old friend.
Oʻtirib gaplashaylik.|Let's sit down and talk.

body.en:
[[-ga qaramay]] = despite, [[-gani sababli]] / [[tufayli]] = because of, thanks to, [[shuning uchun]] = therefore, [[biroq]] = however, [[shunday qilib]] = thus.

[[Qiyinchiliklarga qaramay, loyiha oʻz vaqtida yakunlandi.]]

grammar.ex:
Qiyinchiliklarga qaramay, loyiha oʻz vaqtida yakunlandi.|Despite the difficulties, the project was finished on time.
Yomgʻir yogʻgani sababli, uchrashuv qoldirildi.|Because of the rain, the meeting was postponed.
Shuning uchun biz rejani oʻzgartirdik.|That's why we changed the plan.

title.en: Possible and impossible: mumkin and -ib boʻlmaydi

body.en:
[[-ish mumkin]] = it is possible / allowed: [[Bu yerda suratga olish mumkin.]]

[[-ib boʻlmaydi]] = it is impossible: [[Bitta misoldan xulosa chiqarib boʻlmaydi.]] = One cannot draw conclusions from a single example.

grammar.ex:
Bu yerda suratga olish mumkin.|You may take photos here.
Bitta misoldan xulosa chiqarib boʻlmaydi.|One can't draw conclusions from a single example.
Uning qilmishini oqlab boʻlmaydi.|His act cannot be justified.

readings.title: Raqamli asrda kitob oʻqish
readings.sents:
Soʻnggi paytlarda koʻpchilik odamlar kitob oʻqimay qoʻydi deb noliydi.|Lately many people complain that people have stopped reading.
Biroq tadqiqotlar murakkabroq manzarani koʻrsatmoqda.|However, research shows a more complex picture.
Biz avvalgidan kam oʻqimaymiz, lekin boshqacha oʻqiymiz.|We read no less than before, but we read differently.
Matnlar qisqaroq, diqqat esa tarqoqroq boʻlib qoldi.|Texts have become shorter, and attention more scattered.
Shunday qilib, oʻqishning miqdori emas, chuqurligi zarar koʻrmoqda.|Thus, it is not the quantity but the depth of reading that suffers.
Olimlar diqqatni jamlash qobiliyati — bu koʻnikma ekanini taʼkidlaydi.|Scientists emphasize that the ability to concentrate is a skill.
Har qanday koʻnikma kabi uni mashq qildirish kerak.|Like any skill, it needs to be trained.
Masalan, qogʻoz kitoblarni yonida telefon boʻlmagan holda oʻqish foydali.|For example, it is useful to read paper books without a phone nearby.
Umuman olganda, raqamli texnologiyalarning oʻzi zararli emas.|On the whole, digital technologies are not harmful in themselves.
Hammasi ulardan qanday foydalanishimizga bogʻliq.|Everything depends on how we use them.

readings.title: Barqaror rivojlanish
readings.sents:
Barqaror rivojlanish konsepsiyasi yigirmanchi asr oxirida paydo boʻlgan.|The concept of sustainable development appeared at the end of the twentieth century.
Uning mohiyati oddiy: kelajak avlodlarga zarar yetkazmasdan bugungi ehtiyojlarni qondirish.|Its essence is simple: meet today's needs without harming future generations.
Biroq amalda bu ancha murakkab boʻlib chiqdi.|However, in practice this turned out to be much more difficult.
Iqtisodiy oʻsish koʻpincha atrof-muhitni muhofaza qilishga zid keladi.|Economic growth often contradicts environmental protection.
Shunga qaramay, koʻplab mamlakatlar «yashil» texnologiyalarni joriy etmoqda.|Nevertheless, many countries are introducing "green" technologies.
Kompaniyalar ham ekologik omillarni hisobga olmoqda.|Companies also take environmental factors into account.
Shubhasiz, har birimizning ishtirokimizsiz muvaffaqiyat boʻlmaydi.|Undoubtedly, without the participation of each of us there will be no success.

readings.title: Bahslashish sanʼati
readings.sents:
Bahslasha olish — zamonaviy dunyodagi eng muhim qobiliyatlardan biri.|The ability to argue is one of the most important in the modern world.
Bahsning maqsadi suhbatdoshni yengish emas, balki haqiqatga yaqinlashishdir.|The goal of an argument is not to defeat the other person but to get closer to the truth.
Eng avvalo, raqibni diqqat bilan tinglash kerak.|First of all, you need to listen carefully to your opponent.
Keyin hissiyotlarni emas, dalillarni keltirish kerak.|Then you should give arguments, not emotions.
Faktlarni fikrlardan ajrata bilish muhim.|It is important to distinguish facts from opinions.
Agar notoʻgʻri boʻlsangiz, tan oling — bu zaiflik emas, kuch belgisi.|If you are wrong, admit it — it's a sign of strength, not weakness.
Oxir-oqibat, yaxshi bahs ikkala tomonni ham boyitadi.|Ultimately, a good argument enriches both sides.

A|Sunʼiy intellektning mehnat bozoriga taʼsirini qanday baholaysiz?|How do you assess the impact of artificial intelligence on the labor market?
B|Bir tomondan, u odatiy vazifalarni avtomatlashtiradi.|On the one hand, it automates routine tasks.
B|Boshqa tomondan, yangi kasblar paydo boʻlmoqda.|On the other hand, new professions are emerging.

B|Aynan shuning uchun davlat taʼlimga sarmoya kiritishi kerak.|That's exactly why the state should invest in education.
A|Qoʻshilaman, lekin bu vaqt talab qiladi.|I agree, but it takes time.
B|Albatta. Shuning uchun bugundan boshlash kerak.|Certainly. That's why we must start today.

A|Asosiy masalaga oʻtishni taklif qilaman.|I suggest we move on to the main issue.
B|Ha, shartnoma shartlarini muhokama qilaylik.|Yes, let's discuss the terms of the contract.
A|Yetkazib berish muddatlari bizga toʻgʻri kelmaydi.|The delivery terms do not suit us.
B|Biz ularni bir haftaga qisqartira olamiz.|We can shorten them by a week.
A|Narx-chi?|And what about the price?
B|Katta buyurtma uchun chegirma berishga tayyormiz.|For a large order we are ready to provide a discount.
A|Unday boʻlsa, shartnomani imzolashimiz mumkin.|In that case we can sign the agreement.
B|Ajoyib. Hujjatlarni ertagacha tayyorlayman.|Excellent. I'll prepare the documents by tomorrow.

B|«Jinoyat va jazo»ni qayta oʻqiyapman.|I'm rereading "Crime and Punishment".
A|Juda gʻamgin emasmi?|Isn't it too gloomy?
B|Gʻamgin, lekin chuqur. Har safar yangi narsa topaman.|Gloomy, but deep. Every time I find something new.
A|Unda sizni eng koʻp nima jalb qiladi?|What attracts you most in it?
B|Qahramonlar psixologiyasi va vijdon haqidagi abadiy savollar.|The psychology of the characters and the eternal questions about conscience.
A|Balki men ham uni qayta oʻqishim kerakdir.|Perhaps I should reread it too.

body.en:
A direct quote is closed with [[deb]]: [[U «Ertaga kelaman», deb aytdi.]]

In indirect speech, the verb becomes a noun form with a possessive ending: [[U keyinroq kelishini aytdi.]] = He said he would come later; [[U charchaganini aytdi.]] = He said he was tired.

grammar.ex:
U «Ertaga kelaman», deb aytdi.|He said, "I'll come tomorrow."
U keyinroq kelishini aytdi.|He said he would come later.
U qayerda ishlashimni soʻradi.|He asked where I work.

quiz.en: A direct quote is closed with:

body.en: [[-ku]] = "but I told you!" / emphasis: [[Aytdim-ku!]] — [[-chi]] = "what about…?" or urging: [[Sen-chi?]] (And you?), [[Kelsang-chi!]] (Come on, do come!) — [[-da]] = friendly emphasis: [[Boʻldi-da!]] (That's enough!) — [[-oq]]/[[-yoq]] = "as soon as / even": [[kirishi bilanoq]] = as soon as he entered.

grammar.ex:
Aytdim-ku!|I told you!
Sen-chi?|And you?
U kirishi bilanoq hamma jim boʻldi.|As soon as he came in, everyone fell silent.

readings.title: Sukut sanʼati
readings.sents:
Soʻz kumush boʻlsa, sukut oltin, deyishadi.|They say that speech is silver, but silence is gold.
Cheksiz xabarlar asrida bu maqol deyarli daʼvatdek yangraydi.|In the age of endless messages, this proverb sounds almost like a challenge.
Biz javob berishga, izoh qoldirishga, fikr bildirishga shoshilamiz.|We rush to answer, comment, have our say.
Va kamdan-kam bunga arziganmi, deb oʻylaymiz.|And rarely wonder whether it was worth it.
Holbuki, kerakli paytda jim tura olish zaiflik emas, balki yetuklik belgisidir.|Meanwhile, the ability to keep silent at the right moment is a sign not of weakness but of maturity.
Sukut eshitganlarimizni mushohada qilish uchun vaqt beradi.|Silence gives time to make sense of what was heard.
Maʼlum boʻlishicha, tinglash gapirishdan kam muhim emas.|It turns out that listening is no less important than speaking.
Barcha zamonlarning donishmandlari kamgaplikni qadrlagani bejiz emas.|It is no coincidence that sages of all ages valued taciturnity.

readings.title: Tarjima haqida
readings.sents:
Tarjima — soʻzlarni oddiygina almashtirish emas.|Translation is not a simple replacement of words.
Har bir til oʻzida dunyoga alohida qarashni saqlaydi.|Every language holds within itself a special vision of the world.
Iboralar, soʻz oʻyinlari, ichki maʼno — bularning barchasini tarjima qilish qiyin.|Idioms, wordplay, subtext — all this is hard to translate.
Tarjimon aniqlik va goʻzallik oʻrtasida tanlov qilishiga toʻgʻri keladi.|A translator has to choose between accuracy and beauty.
Tarjimonni hammuallif deyishlari bejiz emas.|No wonder they say a translator is a co-author.
Yaxshi tarjima nafaqat maʼnoni, balki asl nusxaning ruhini ham saqlaydi.|A good translation preserves not only the meaning but also the spirit of the original.
Aynan shuning uchun buyuk kitoblar qayta-qayta tarjima qilinadi.|That is precisely why great books are translated again and again.

readings.title: Joy xotirasi
readings.sents:
Shunday shaharlar borki, biz ulardan ketganimizdan keyin ham uzoq vaqt ichimizda yashaydi.|There are cities that live in us long after we have left them.
Eski koʻchadagi yomgʻir hidi, qoʻngʻiroqlar jarangi, bozordagi savdogarning ovozi.|The smell of rain on an old street, the ringing of bells, the voice of a merchant at the market.
Bularning barchasi toʻsatdan xotirada jonlanadi.|All this suddenly surfaces in memory.
Nostalgiya — shunchaki oʻtmishni sogʻinish emas.|Nostalgia is not just longing for the past.
Bu — u yerda qolib ketgan oʻzligingning bir qismini qaytarishga urinish.|It is an attempt to bring back a part of yourself that stayed there.
Yillar oʻtib u yerga qaytganimizda, koʻpincha na shaharni, na oʻzimizni taniymiz.|Returning there years later, we often recognize neither the city nor ourselves.
Shunga qaramay, bu uchrashuv gʻalati bir osoyishtalik bagʻishlaydi.|And yet this meeting gives a strange serenity.

dialogues.lines:
A|Xoʻsh, romanni oʻqib tugatdingmi?|So, did you finish the novel?
B|Tugatdim. Rostini aytsam, yakuni meni esankiratib qoʻydi.|I did. Honestly, the ending baffled me.
A|Ha, muallif gapni oxiriga yetkazmaslikni yaxshi koʻradi.|Yes, the author likes to leave things unsaid.
B|Aynan. Hammasi ichki maʼnoga asoslangan.|Exactly. Everything rests on the subtext.
A|Lekin tili qanday! Qoʻlimdan qoʻya olmadim.|But what language! I couldn't put it down.
B|Bu toʻgʻri, bahslashib boʻlmaydi.|That's true, no arguing.

A|Hali ham mendan xafamisan?|Are you still offended with me?
B|Xafa emas, koʻproq hafsalam pir boʻldi.|Not so much offended as disappointed.
A|Tushunaman. Jahl ustida ortiqcha gapirib yubordim.|I understand. I lost my temper and said too much.
B|Otilgan oʻq qaytmas, aytilgan soʻz qaytmas.|A word is not a sparrow; once it flies out, you can't catch it.
A|Bilaman. Iltimos, meni kechir.|I know. Please forgive me.
B|Mayli, oʻtgan ishga salovat.|All right, let bygones be bygones.
A|Rahmat. Sen haqiqiy doʻstsan.|Thank you. You're a true friend.

A|Bu kartina haqida nima deysan?|What do you say about this canvas?
B|Rangi hayratlanarli, lekin menimcha, kompozitsiyasi juda yuklangan.|The colors are striking, but the composition is overloaded, in my opinion.
A|Menimcha esa, rassomning niyati aynan shunda.|And I think that's exactly the artist's intention.
B|Ehtimol. Tartibsizlik — davr aksi sifatidami?|Possibly. Chaos as a reflection of the era?
A|Aynan. Moʻyqalam izlariga qara — ularda qanchalik xavotir bor.|Exactly. Look at the brushstrokes — how much anxiety there is in them.
B|Meni deyarli ishontirding.|You've almost convinced me.
